claims.statement: An LPDDR5X data net is normally point to point, controller to DRAM, with no fly-by topology; a dual-rank or two-die configuration puts more than one device on it, and a CAMM2 module adds a connector.
claims.source: Synopsys LPDDR5 technical bulletin and LPDDR5X/5/4X controller documentation, on rank and dual-channel support; byte-mode descriptions of two 8-bit dies on one 16-bit channel
claims.conditions: Single-rank, single-die is the common case; rank count and byte mode change the loading
claims.note: Corrected. "Point to point rather than multidrop" was too strong: LPDDR5 defines non-target ODT precisely because a dual-rank configuration exists, and a device may be built as two 8-bit dies sharing one 16-bit channel. The page already says so — it calls "never multi-drop" a step too far and tells the reader to check the configuration — so this row now matches what the page claims rather than what it used to. 18 Oct 2026: CAMM2 (JESD318, C-54) puts LPDDR5/5X on a compression-attached module, so "no connector" is no longer universal; the page now says so.
claims.source_title: Synopsys — Key features designers should know about LPDDR5

claims.statement: LPDDR5 and LPDDR5X have no bidirectional DQS: WCK, forwarded by the controller, times writes and an optional RDQS from the DRAM times reads; CK runs at a quarter of the WCK frequency above 3200 Mbps and half of it below.

claims.conditions: LPDDR5 and its LPDDR5X extension; single-ended or strobe-less reads are allowed at low speed
claims.note: Read on synopsys.com. The bulletin gives CK at 800 MHz for 6400 Mbps, command/address at double data rate on CK, and says a differential RDQS becomes necessary at higher speeds. Scoped because it is an IP vendor’s description of JESD209-5, which JEDEC sells.
claims.source_title: Synopsys — Key features designers should know about LPDDR5

claims.statement: LPDDR5/5X bring-up runs Vref training, command (CA) training, WCK2CK leveling and then WCK-to-DQ read and write training; LPDDR5X adds receiver offset calibration.
claims.source: Cadence blogs (S. Sharma): "Device Training for High Speed DRAMs", 12 April 2022; "Taking LPDDR5 to the Next Level", 19 February 2021
claims.conditions: The categories a verification-IP vendor lists; the exact sequence and its timing are in JESD209-5, and a controller may order or repeat steps differently
claims.note: Re-sourced from an unread normative reference to two free Cadence articles. The older statement, that training centres the strobe in the eye, is the last of these steps. Offset calibration training is from the 2021 article, which says it is recommended at every power-up and initialisation.
claims.source_title: Cadence — Device training for high-speed DRAMs

IP vendors implementing it, not the Base text.
claims.source_title: Cadence — Unravelling PCIe 6.0 FLIT mode challenges

claims.statement: An M-PHY burst requires re-acquisition from a preamble.
claims.source: Mixel, "M-PHY benefits and challenges"; Synopsys M-PHY article, on HS-BURST structure and STALL
claims.conditions: HS-MODE; STALL is the power-saving state between bursts
claims.note: Confirmed by the burst structure: an HS-BURST is PREPARE, SYNC, MARKERs and then data, where SYNC is the symbol sequence the receiver uses to bit-synchronise to the embedded clock. Between bursts the lane sits in STALL with activity stopped, so each burst re-acquires. That is the mechanism the page describes.
claims.source_title: Mixel — M-PHY benefits and challenges

claims.statement: Every USB 3.2 port must use spread-spectrum clocking: down-spread at a modulation rate of 30 to 33 kHz, with a peak deviation between -4000 and -5000 ppm. The profile is vendor-specific, and the rate of change is limited to 1250 ppm/us.

The earlier commercial source (TI SDAA423) agreed on 30 to 33 kHz. Re-sourced to the specification on 18 Oct 2026.
claims.source_title: USB-IF — Universal Serial Bus 3.2 Specification, Revision 1.1 (June 2022)

claims.statement: The DC bias dependence of the same nominal MLCC part differs markedly between vendors, and X7R is not reliably less bias-sensitive than X5R.

claims.conditions: 1 uF 0603 16 V parts from six vendors in X5R and X7R; DC stepped 0.2 V over -20 to +20 V; AC 10 mVrms and 500 mVrms
claims.note: Read from the paper's own conclusions, not from its plotted curves. The authors anonymise the vendors, which is why this site names no part's derating curve. This claim is the reason the panel takes the retained fraction as an input. Retrieved 12 September 2026 from the authors' paper archive. The link is http, not https: the https endpoint on that host returns 404, so an upgraded URL silently fails.
claims.source_title: Novak et al. — DC and AC Bias Dependence of MLCC Capacitors, DesignCon East 2011

Recorded because it is a measured finding being used as a modelling licence. Retrieved 12 September 2026 from the authors' paper archive. Retrieved 12 September 2026 from the authors' paper archive. The link is http, not https: the https endpoint on that host returns 404, so an upgraded URL silently fails.
claims.source_title: Novak et al. — DC and AC Bias Dependence of MLCC Capacitors, DesignCon East 2011

claims.statement: A successive-approximation converter compares against its reference once per bit trial, so a reference that moves during a conversion weighs the early bits differently from the late ones.
claims.source: Analog Devices, "Voltage Reference Design for Precision Successive-Approximation ADCs"
claims.conditions: Charge-redistribution SAR with a single reference node; trial timing within one sample period
claims.note: States the mechanism directly: the reference is disturbed when the DAC inputs change, the DAC changes on each bit-test clock cycle, and the largest droop is at the MSB trial because that capacitor is the largest. That is exactly what this lab models. It describes charge-redistribution SAR parts; the lab’s trial TIMING within the sample period is a modelling choice and the page says so.
claims.source_title: Analog Devices — Voltage reference design for precision SAR ADCs

claims.statement: A one-bit delta-sigma modulator's feedback DAC is scaled by the reference, so reference ripple multiplies the bitstream rather than adding to the signal.
claims.source: Analog Devices sigma-delta ADC tutorial and AN-0979, on the one-bit feedback DAC and its reference
claims.conditions: Discrete-time, second order, one bit, single reference; not a continuous-time or multi-bit loop
claims.note: The one-bit feedback DAC switching between levels set by the reference is standard in the published descriptions of this topology, which is what makes reference ripple multiply the bitstream rather than add to the signal. Scoped rather than verified because the page now bounds the behaviour to the loop it simulates — discrete-time, second order, one bit — and says a continuous-time or multi-bit modulator will differ.
claims.source_title: Analog Devices — Sigma-delta ADC tutorial

claims.statement: Counting interference as noise, with the fundamental, DC and harmonics 2 to 6 excluded, is the usual convention for a converter dynamic test.
claims.source: Analog Devices MT-003 tutorial, "Understand SINAD, ENOB, SNR, THD, THD+N and SFDR"
claims.conditions: A coherent single-tone FFT test; exclusion widths depend on the window
claims.note: MT-003 defines SNR as the signal against all other spectral components below Nyquist EXCLUDING harmonics and DC, and SINAD as including harmonics but excluding DC. That is the convention this lab declares. The specific choices — harmonics 2 to 6, plus or minus 4 bins, Blackman-Harris — are this lab’s parameters, published in its result contract, not a standard’s requirement. IEEE Std 1241 has not been read and the page makes no compliance claim.
claims.source_title: Analog Devices MT-003 — Understand SINAD, ENOB, SNR, THD, THD+N and SFDR

claims.statement: Input-referred coupling appears as an offset error, a constant reference error as a gain error, and a reference that changes during the bit trials as a linearity error.
claims.source: Derived on this page from the converter model, and measured with it: offset 0.90 mV, gain −0.318 dBFS implying a 2.41 V effective reference, and THD rising to −53.5 dB
claims.conditions: Ideal SAR, shared converter clock so the disturbance repeats per conversion
claims.note: Narrowed in this batch: DNL and INL are named as the mechanism and explicitly not measured, because the lab runs no static ramp or histogram test and THD is not a substitute for one. The resemblance to a static nonlinearity holds only while the disturbance repeats in step with the conversions, which the page now says.

claims.statement: A sinc-cubed decimator is the usual filter after a second-order modulator, and it nulls exactly at multiples of the output data rate.
claims.source: Analog Devices AN-0979, "Digital Filtering Options", and the sigma-delta ADC tutorial
claims.conditions: Three cascaded length-OSR moving averages, decimating by OSR
claims.note: Better than "the usual choice": there is a stated design rule. The sinc order should be at least one more than the modulator order to keep out-of-band noise from aliasing back, which puts a second-order modulator at sinc-cubed, and the notch position follows the output data rate directly. Both halves of the claim, from the manufacturer’s own filter documentation.
claims.source_title: Analog Devices AN-0979 — Digital filtering options

claims.conditions: 64 GT/s PAM4, measured through the specified test setup
claims.note: Teledyne LeCroy (27 June 2022) calls RLM and SNDR “two new measurements introduced in PCIe 6.0”. A modelling vendor quotes limits that differ from those an earlier version of this page gave; neither has been read against the Base specification, so the page gives none.
claims.source_title: Teledyne LeCroy — Get Ready for PCIe 6.0 Base Tx Testing

claims.statement: JESD79-5C (April 2024) extended DDR5 timing definitions to 8800 MT/s.
claims.source: JEDEC press release, "JEDEC Updates JESD79-5C DDR5 SDRAM Standard", 17 April 2024
claims.source_title: JEDEC — JESD79-5C DDR5 SDRAM standard update announcement
claims.conditions: The standard's timing definitions; says nothing about which bins a part or platform supports
claims.note: Read on jedec.org: timing parameters expanded from 6800 to 8800 Mbps, with DRAM core and Tx/Rx AC timings to 8800.

claims.statement: The current DDR5 edition is JESD79-5D, published November 2025.
claims.source: JEDEC document page for JESD79-5D, Version 1.41
claims.source_title: JEDEC — JESD79-5D DDR5 SDRAM document page
claims.conditions: Edition and date only
claims.note: Read on jedec.org. The standard is sold ($423 to non-members) and its contents have not been read; every electrical value on the page comes from vendor documents and is labelled so.

claims.statement: DDR5 runs VDD = VDDQ = 1.1 V and VPP = 1.8 V, with pseudo-open-drain I/O; DDR4 ran 1.2/1.2/2.5 V.
claims.source: Micron DDR5 SDRAM core data sheet, Rev. D 10/2022 (stated JESD79-5B compliant); Micron white paper "Introducing Micron DDR5 SDRAM: More Than a Generational Update", table 1
claims.source_title: Micron — DDR5 SDRAM core data sheet (Rev. D, JESD79-5B compliant)
claims.conditions: Nominal values
claims.note: Both documents give the same values and describe the DQ bus as single-ended POD.

claims.statement: DDR5 DRAM ODT values are 240, 120, 80, 60, 48, 40 and 34 ohm (RZQ/1 to RZQ/7, RZQ = 240 ohm) or off, programmed separately as RTT_WR, RTT_NOM_WR, RTT_NOM_RD and RTT_PARK; the output driver is 34, 40 or 48 ohm.
claims.source: Micron DDR5 SDRAM core data sheet, Rev. D 10/2022 (stated JESD79-5B compliant), MR34, MR35 and the output driver mode register
claims.source_title: Micron — DDR5 SDRAM core data sheet (Rev. D, JESD79-5B compliant)
claims.conditions: DQ ODT and driver impedance
claims.note: Read from the mode register tables. The page's table of which value applies when follows the data sheet's description of command-based non-target ODT and park termination.

claims.statement: VrefDQ is internal, set from 35% to 97.5% of VDDQ in 0.5% steps, default 75%.
claims.source: Micron DDR5 SDRAM core data sheet, Rev. D 10/2022 (stated JESD79-5B compliant), MR10 and the internal VrefDQ specification table
claims.source_title: Micron — DDR5 SDRAM core data sheet (Rev. D, JESD79-5B compliant)
claims.conditions: Nominal step; the step tolerance is 0.41% to 0.59%
claims.note: The page uses the nominal 0.5% step (5.5 mV at 1.1 V).

claims.statement: The DDR5 DRAM has a 4-tap DFE on its DQ inputs; at 3200-6400 MT/s tap 1 spans -200 to +50 mV, tap 2 +/-75, tap 3 +/-60 and tap 4 +/-45 mV in 5 mV steps, with gain of +/-6 dB in 2 dB steps, and the stressed-eye test requires |t2| + |t3| + |t4| < 60 mV.
claims.source: Micron DDR5 SDRAM core data sheet, Rev. D 10/2022 (stated JESD79-5B compliant), Decision Feedback Equalization, tables 233 and 234, and the Rx stressed eye notes
claims.source_title: Micron — DDR5 SDRAM core data sheet (Rev. D, JESD79-5B compliant)
claims.conditions: 1X tap multiplier; 6800-8800 values are TBD in this revision
claims.note: Read from the data sheet. The data sheet notes these ranges are for relative evaluation and that absolute values are not production tested; the panel uses them as limits.

claims.statement: The DRAM receiver is tested with a stressed eye at the slicer, after the DFE: 95 mV by 0.25 UI at 3200 MT/s down to 57.5 mV by 0.23 UI at 6400, with the higher bins TBD in that revision.
claims.source: Micron DDR5 SDRAM core data sheet, Rev. D 10/2022 (stated JESD79-5B compliant), tables 321 and 322
claims.source_title: Micron — DDR5 SDRAM core data sheet (Rev. D, JESD79-5B compliant)
claims.conditions: Golden reference channel, with injected jitter and noise, BER 1e-16 by extrapolation from 1e-9
claims.note: The page states plainly that this is a receiver test condition, not a channel mask, and draws it only up to 6400.

claims.statement: DDR5's raw BER requirement is 1e-16 per lane in operation; receiver and transmitter limits are validated at 1e-9, needing 5.3e9 UI at 99.5% confidence.
claims.source: Micron DDR5 SDRAM core data sheet, Rev. D 10/2022 (stated JESD79-5B compliant), Minimum BER Requirements, table 277
claims.source_title: Micron — DDR5 SDRAM core data sheet (Rev. D, JESD79-5B compliant)
claims.conditions: Raw BER per lane, before correction
claims.note: The 5.3e9 figure is also derived on the page from -ln(0.005)/1e-9 and checked by check-numbers.py.

claims.statement: DDR5 modules route command, address and clock fly-by from the RCD, and data and strobes point to point; write leveling compensates the resulting CK-to-DQS skew at each DRAM, and DDR5 adds an internal cycle alignment step for the DRAM's unmatched internal path.
claims.source: Micron DDR5 SDRAM core data sheet, Rev. D 10/2022 (stated JESD79-5B compliant), Write Leveling Training Mode; Micron technical brief "DDR5: Key Module Features"
claims.source_title: Micron — DDR5 SDRAM core data sheet (Rev. D, JESD79-5B compliant)
claims.conditions: RDIMM; a UDIMM is fly-by from the controller
claims.note: The data sheet describes external leveling to the phase and cycle of CWL and the WICA internal alignment; the page's figure follows its description.

claims.statement: A DDR5 DIMM has two independent subchannels, each 32 data bits plus 8 for ECC on an ECC module; with burst length 16 one subchannel delivers 64 bytes.
claims.source: Micron technical brief "DDR5: Key Module Features"; Micron white paper "DDR5 SDRAM: New Features"
claims.source_title: Micron — DDR5: Key Module Features (technical brief)
claims.conditions: Standard modules; BL32 exists for x4 devices
claims.note: Both documents state the 40-bit subchannels and the BL16 to 64-byte relation.

claims.statement: DDR5 adds CS and CA training, internal write leveling, read training patterns including an LFSR pattern, a duty-cycle adjuster and a DQS interval oscillator; on-die ECC is single-error correction over 128 data and 8 parity bits; CRC covers reads as well as writes.
claims.source: Micron white papers "Introducing Micron DDR5 SDRAM" (table 1) and "DDR5 SDRAM: New Features"
claims.source_title: Micron — Introducing Micron DDR5 SDRAM: More Than a Generational Update
claims.conditions: Feature list
claims.note: Read from the comparison table and the RAS section.

claims.statement: On an RDIMM the host sends 7 CA pins per subchannel at double data rate to the RCD, which drives the DRAMs' 14 CA pins at single data rate; the DDR5 RDIMM edge has more VSS pins than DDR4's.
claims.source: Micron technical brief "DDR5: Key Module Features", table 1 and the CAI section
claims.source_title: Micron — DDR5: Key Module Features (technical brief)
claims.conditions: L/RDIMM
claims.note: The brief gives 2 x 7 DDR CA pins, a 14-pin SDR DRAM CA bus, and 127 VSS pins against 94.

claims.statement: The PMIC on a DDR5 module regulates the DRAM rails from a 12 V input on RDIMMs and 5 V on UDIMMs and SODIMMs.
claims.source: Micron technical brief "DDR5: Key Module Features" and white paper "DDR5: Client Module Features", pin tables
claims.source_title: Micron — DDR5: Client Module Features
claims.conditions: Bulk input pins
claims.note: Read from the two pin-difference tables.

claims.statement: DDR5 DRAMs terminate CA, CS and CK on die, and a CA_ODT strap selects group A (weak or off, typically for DRAMs along the chain) or group B (strong, 40 or 80 ohm, for the last DRAM of the fly-by).
claims.source: Micron white paper "DDR5: Client Module Features", DDR5 On-Die Termination; Micron DDR5 SDRAM core data sheet, Rev. D 10/2022 (stated JESD79-5B compliant), MR32/MR33
claims.source_title: Micron — DDR5: Client Module Features
claims.conditions: UDIMM/SODIMM description; RDIMMs also terminate on die
claims.note: The white paper gives the group A/B usage; the data sheet gives the CA ODT values.

claims.statement: DDR5 has 8 to 64 Gb device densities, a 16n prefetch, and doubles DDR4's bank groups.
claims.source: Micron white paper "Introducing Micron DDR5 SDRAM", table 1
claims.source_title: Micron — Introducing Micron DDR5 SDRAM: More Than a Generational Update
claims.conditions: As published in 2019; JESD79-5D's abstract covers 8 to 32 Gb devices
claims.note: Not stated on the page as numbers; kept so the comparison table's omissions are deliberate. The 64 Gb figure is the white paper's; JEDEC's current abstract says 8 to 32 Gb.

claims.statement: JEDEC's clocked UDIMM and SODIMM (JESD323, JESD324, published 2024) put a clock driver (CKD) on the module that regenerates the clock locally; JEDEC presents it as raising client DIMM data rates from 6400 to 7200 Mbps in the initial version, targeting up to 9200 in future versions.
claims.source: JEDEC press release, "JEDEC to Launch New Raw Card DIMM Designs with DDR5 Clock Drivers, Enhancing Client Computing Memory Performance and Stability at 6400 Mbps and Beyond", 15 October 2024
claims.source_title: JEDEC — DDR5 clock driver (CUDIMM, CSODIMM) raw card announcement
claims.conditions: Client modules; the CKD buffers the clock only
claims.note: Re-sourced 22 Oct 2026 from an EDN report to JEDEC's own release, read on jedec.org. The release names JESD323 and JESD324 as published earlier in 2024. The page says the CKD regenerates the clock and that command and address still come from the controller.

claims.statement: Board makers' manuals name the slot to fill first with one DIMM per channel; ASUS's FAQ says DIMM_A2 and gives no reason.
claims.source: ASUS support FAQ 1049387, "How to install DRAM (memory) on motherboard"
claims.source_title: ASUS — How to install DRAM (memory) on motherboard
claims.conditions: Consumer boards; slot naming and routing are board specific
claims.note: The FAQ gives the slot, not the reason. The page offers the stub argument from its own model as a likely reason for a daisy-chained layout and tells the reader to follow the manual.

claims.statement: Lenovo's ThinkSystem SR650 V3 runs DDR5 at a lower rate with two DIMMs per channel than with one: 4800 against 4400 MT/s with 4th Gen Xeon processors, 5600 against 4800 MT/s with 5th Gen.
claims.source: Lenovo Press LP1601, ThinkSystem SR650 V3 product guide
claims.conditions: One platform, as an example of the practice; other platforms set their own population rules
claims.note: The product guide: “Supports 1 DIMM per channel operating at 5600 MHz (5th Gen processors) or 4800 MHz (4th Gen processors). Supports 2 DIMMs per channel operating at 4800 MHz (5th Gen processors) or 4400 MHz (4th Gen processors).” The page quotes the 4th Gen pair as an example.
claims.source_title: Lenovo Press — ThinkSystem SR650 V3 product guide

claims.statement: LPDDR5X has a x16 channel per die, LVSTL I/O at a VDDQ of 0.5 V (0.45 V option, 0.3 V with ODT off), a differential WCK data clock at 2:1 or 4:1 to CK, an optional read strobe RDQS, and optional DRAM-side DFE and pre-emphasis advertised in mode registers.
claims.source: Micron 315b x32 Automotive LPDDR5X SDRAM data sheet, Rev. B 11/2022: features, and product-specific mode registers MR0 and MR24
claims.source_title: Micron — x32 Automotive LPDDR5X SDRAM data sheet (315b)
claims.conditions: One vendor family; DFE and pre-emphasis support vary by device
claims.note: Read from the features page and the mode register table: MR0 OP[6] pre-emphasis supported, OP[7] per-pin DFE not supported, MR24 OP[7] DFE supported (a 3-step DFE). The page says only that equalisation is optional and advertised per device.

claims.statement: JEDEC JESD318 (December 2023) defines CAMM2 modules for both DDR5 and LPDDR5/5X on a common connector with different pinouts, and aims LPDDR5/5X CAMM2s at notebooks and some server segments; mounting differs on purpose, so a module cannot be fitted where the other kind belongs.
claims.source: JEDEC press release, "JEDEC Publishes New CAMM2 Memory Module Standard", 5 December 2023
claims.source_title: JEDEC — CAMM2 memory module standard announcement
claims.conditions: The announcement; the standard itself has not been read
claims.note: Read on jedec.org; re-read 19 Oct 2026 for the mounting detail. The release also describes stackable single-channel CAMM2s, with DDR5 examples.

claims.statement: JESD209-6 (LPDDR6) was published on 9 July 2025: two sub-channels per die with 12 DQ and 4 CA each, on-the-fly burst length for 32- and 64-byte access, static and dynamic efficiency modes, dynamic write NT-ODT, two mandatory VDD2 supplies, DVFSL, PRAC, programmable link protection, on-die ECC and CA parity.
claims.source: JEDEC press release, "JEDEC Releases New LPDDR6 Standard to Enhance Mobile and AI Memory Performance", 9 July 2025
claims.source_title: JEDEC — LPDDR6 (JESD209-6) announcement
claims.conditions: The announcement; the standard itself has not been read
claims.note: Read on jedec.org. The release gives no data rates; those are C-58. Re-read 23 Oct 2026: the release quotes the JC-42.6 vice-chair naming edge AI computing, client computers, data centres and automotive as fields LPDDR6 will reach beyond mobile.

claims.statement: LPDDR6 runs CK at 2667 MHz (LPDDR5X 1066.5 MHz) with only a 2:1 WCK:CK ratio; VDD1/VDD2C/VDD2D/VDDQ are 1.8/1.0/0.875/0.5 V (0.3 V VDDQ option); 16 banks and BL24/48 per sub-channel; LVSTL I/O with DQ ODT to VSSQ; a burst is 12 DQ x 24 = 288 bits, 256 data + 16 metadata + 16 DBI or link ECC/EDC, with no DMI pin.
claims.source: Samsung (Seunghyun Moon), "LPDDR6 Key Architecture", JEDEC LPDDR6 Workshop, 8 April 2025
claims.source_title: Samsung — LPDDR6 Key Architecture (JEDEC workshop)
claims.conditions: A member presentation at JEDEC’s workshop, after the content was balloted; not the standard
claims.note: Read from the comparison table and the metadata slides. The LPDDR5X column of the same table gives 9600 Mbps, which the page attributes to vendor material.

claims.statement: LPDDR6 adopted wide NRZ (12 DQ per sub-channel) rather than PAM4; Samsung’s workshop presentation puts PAM4 at about half the signal-integrity margin and about 1.5 times the I/O power for the same bandwidth.
claims.source: Samsung, "LPDDR6 Key Architecture", JEDEC LPDDR6 Workshop, April 2025, slide "High Bandwidth – Wide NRZ"
claims.source_title: Samsung — LPDDR6 Key Architecture (JEDEC workshop)
claims.conditions: An attributed comparison, not a measurement the page repeats
claims.note: The page states it as Samsung’s framing and shows its own model reaches the same ordering.

claims.statement: LPDDR6 starts at 10.667 Gb/s per pin and its highest defined rate is 14.4 Gb/s.
claims.source: Synopsys, "LPDDR6: A Deep Dive Into the JEDEC Press Release", JEDEC forum, May 2024; Synopsys blog "Delivering LPDDR6 read/write eyes at 10.67 Gb/s", January 2026; Cadence technical article, September 2025
claims.source_title: Synopsys — Delivering LPDDR6 read/write eyes at 10.67 Gb/s
claims.conditions: IP vendors’ statements of the standard’s rates
claims.note: Consistent across Synopsys (2024 and 2026) and Cadence (2025, PHY at 14.4 Gb/s); JEDEC’s own release states no rates, so the page attributes them to IP vendors.

claims.statement: On LPDDR6 each DBI flag covers 16 data bits, the 16 extra bits carry DBI or link protection but not both, and a new shared ALERT pin reports faults such as write link errors to the host.
claims.source: Synopsys, "LPDDR6: A Deep Dive Into the JEDEC Press Release", JEDEC forum, May 2024 (based on ballots as of March 2024)
claims.source_title: Synopsys — LPDDR6 deep dive (JEDEC forum, 2024)
claims.conditions: Before the standard was final
claims.note: The deck says it may change; Samsung’s 2025 deck confirms the 16 DBI-or-link bits and ALERT. The DBI inversion rule the packet panel uses, invert above half ones, is the purpose of DC DBI on a ground-terminated bus, not a quoted rule.

claims.statement: SK hynix announced a 1c-process 16 Gb LPDDR6 DRAM in March 2026, with a base speed over 10.7 Gb/s, 33% faster and more than 20% lower power than LPDDR5X, and supply from the second half of 2026.
claims.source: SK hynix newsroom, "SK hynix Develops 1c LPDDR6", 10 March 2026
claims.source_title: SK hynix — 1c LPDDR6 development
claims.conditions: A vendor announcement
claims.note: Re-read 23 Oct 2026 on news.skhynix.com. The release attributes the power saving to the sub-channel structure and DVFS, and says mass-production preparation was to finish in the first half of the year. Trade-press reports of a 14.4 Gb/s target are not used.

claims.statement: LPDDR6 PHYs use receive DFE and ODT tuning, and trained read and write eyes have been shown at 10.67 Gb/s.
claims.source: Synopsys blog, "Delivering LPDDR6 read/write eyes at 10.67 Gb/s", January 2026
claims.source_title: Synopsys — Delivering LPDDR6 read/write eyes at 10.67 Gb/s
claims.conditions: One IP vendor’s PHY
claims.note: The blog gives no eye dimensions or tap counts; the page claims none.

claims.statement: GDDR7 (JESD239, March 2024) uses PAM3 signalling.
claims.source: JEDEC press release, "JEDEC Publishes GDDR7 Graphics Memory Standard", 5 March 2024
claims.source_title: JEDEC — GDDR7 announcement
claims.conditions: The announcement
claims.note: Read on jedec.org: three levels, three bits over two cycles.

claims.statement: LPDDR5 runs CK at 800 MHz with a WCK:CK ratio of 2:1 up to 3200 Mbps or 4:1, 7 command pins and 16 DQ per channel, BL16/32, VDD2 1.05 V (0.9 V) and VDDQ 0.5 V (0.3 V), and carries DM, DBI or link ECC on two DMI pins.
claims.source: Samsung (Seunghyun Moon), "LPDDR6 Key Architecture", JEDEC LPDDR6 Workshop, 8 April 2025, key spec comparison and metadata slides
claims.source_title: Samsung — LPDDR6 Key Architecture (JEDEC workshop)
claims.conditions: The LPDDR5 column of a member presentation’s comparison table
claims.note: Read from the same table as C-56; the 6400 MT/s rate is also C-2b.

claims.statement: UCIe defines data rates of 4, 8, 12, 16, 24 and 32 GT/s, and UCIe 3.0 adds 48 and 64 GT/s, for both UCIe-S and UCIe-A; UCIe-3D runs up to 4 GT/s.
claims.source: UCIe Consortium overview deck (2025), Key Metrics with UCIe 3.0
claims.conditions: Planar packages; 3D separately
claims.note: Key-metrics table: 'Data Rate (GT/s) 4, 8, 12, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64', 'Up to 4' for UCIe-3D, 'Added 48G and 64G with UCIe 3.0'.
claims.source_title: UCIe Consortium — overview deck, 2025, with the key metrics for UCIe 3.0

claims.statement: A UCIe module (cluster) is 16 lanes wide on a standard package, 64 on an advanced package and 80 for UCIe-3D; a UCIe-S x16 at 32 GT/s carries 512 Gb/s per direction, against 1024 for PCIe 6.0 x16.
claims.source: UCIe Consortium overview deck (2025), Key Metrics with UCIe 3.0
claims.conditions: Main band; sideband excluded
claims.note: Key-metrics table, 'Width (each cluster) 16 64 80'; interface-bandwidth slide, 'UCIe-S x16 512 Gb/s/dir main @ 32G' and 'PCIe6.0 x16 1024 Gb/s/dir'.
claims.source_title: UCIe Consortium — overview deck, 2025, with the key metrics for UCIe 3.0

claims.statement: Bump pitch is 100-130 um for UCIe-S, 25-55 um for UCIe-A, and 10 um or less (optimized) or 10-25 um (functional) for UCIe-3D, which must support hybrid bonding.
claims.source: UCIe Consortium overview deck (2025), Key Metrics with UCIe 3.0
claims.conditions: Consortium targets
claims.note: Key-metrics table, 'Bump Pitch (um) 100 130 25 55 < 10 (optimized) > 10 25 (functional)', 'UCIe-3D must support hybrid bonding'. The table's inequality glyphs are underlined, i.e. at most, not strictly under.
claims.source_title: UCIe Consortium — overview deck, 2025, with the key metrics for UCIe 3.0

claims.statement: Channel reach is up to 25 mm for UCIe-S and up to 2 mm for UCIe-A; UCIe-3D is vertical.
claims.source: UCIe Consortium overview deck (2025), Key Metrics with UCIe 3.0
claims.conditions: Main band
claims.note: Key-metrics table, 'Channel Reach (mm) < 25 < 2 3D vertical'. The glyphs are underlined, i.e. at most.
claims.source_title: UCIe Consortium — overview deck, 2025, with the key metrics for UCIe 3.0

claims.statement: Shoreline bandwidth is 28-224 GB/s/mm for UCIe-S and 165-1317 GB/s/mm for UCIe-A across 4-32 GT/s, and 278/370 and 1975/2634 GB/s/mm at 48/64 GT/s, for 110 um (UCIe-S) and 45 um (UCIe-A) pitches.
claims.source: UCIe Consortium overview deck (2025), Key Metrics with UCIe 3.0
claims.conditions: Reference pitches as stated. Both directions together: the deck does not say so, but the module sizes in C-76 reproduce the table only that way.
claims.note: Key-metrics table, 'BW Shoreline (GB/s/mm) 28 224 278, 370 165 1317 1975, 2634', 'Numbers are for 45u (UCIe-A) and 110u (UCIe-S)'.
claims.source_title: UCIe Consortium — overview deck, 2025, with the key metrics for UCIe 3.0

claims.statement: Power-efficiency targets: UCIe-S 0.5 pJ/b at or below 16 GT/s and 0.75 at or above 32 GT/s; UCIe-A 0.25 at or below 12 GT/s, 0.3 from 16 to 32 GT/s and 0.5 at or above 48 GT/s; UCIe-3D under 0.05 pJ/b at 9 um.
claims.source: UCIe Consortium overview deck (2025), Key Metrics with UCIe 3.0
claims.conditions: Targets, not measurements; no UCIe-S figure at 24 GT/s
claims.note: Key-metrics table, 'Power Efficiency Target (pJ/b) 0.5 (<=16 G) 0.75 (>= 32 G) 0.25 (<=12G) 0.3 (16G 32G) 0.5 (>= 48G) <0.05 at 9 um'.
claims.source_title: UCIe Consortium — overview deck, 2025, with the key metrics for UCIe 3.0

claims.statement: At 48 and 64 GT/s UCIe 3.0 signals NRZ, unidirectional, with quarter-rate clocking; receiver termination is required on both UCIe-S and UCIe-A; equalization is a 3-tap TX FFE, a first-order passive RX CTLE and an optional 1-tap RX DFE; the BER is 1e-15 at 48 GT/s and 1e-12 at 64 GT/s, with CRC and replay.
claims.source: UCIe Consortium overview deck (2025) and UCIe 3.0 white paper
claims.conditions: 48 and 64 GT/s only
claims.note: Deck: 'Signaling: NRZ Uni-directional', 'Clocking: Quarter rate for 48/64 GT/s', 'BER: 10-15 for 48 GT/s and 10-12 for 64 GT/s', 'Termination: RX Termination required for both UCIe-S and UCIe-A', '3-tap TX FFE (1-pre + 1-post); 1st order (passive) RX CTLE', 'Optional 1-tap RX DFE'. The 3.0 white paper repeats the BER, CRC and replay, and equalization.
claims.source_title: UCIe Consortium — UCIe 3.0 white paper

claims.statement: UCIe-3D areal bandwidth density is about 4 TB/s/mm2 at a 9 um pitch and about 300 TB/s/mm2 at 1 um.
claims.source: UCIe Consortium overview deck (2025), Key Metrics with UCIe 3.0
claims.conditions: Hybrid bonding
claims.note: Key-metrics table, 'BW Density (GB/s/mm2) ... 4,000 (9 um) 300,000 (1 um)'.
claims.source_title: UCIe Consortium — overview deck, 2025, with the key metrics for UCIe 3.0

claims.statement: The UCIe forwarded clock runs at 16 GHz for 64 GT/s and 12 GHz for 48 GT/s (quarter rate, the only option there); at 24 and 32 GT/s the table lists both a half-rate and a quarter-rate clock, and from 4 to 16 GT/s half rate only. Half-rate clocks are listed with phases of 90 and 270 degrees, quarter-rate with 45 and 135. Deskew is required from 12 GT/s up and optional at 4 and 8 GT/s.
claims.source: UCIe Consortium overview deck (2025)
claims.conditions: Planar packages
claims.note: Deck table 'Forward Clock Frequency and Phase', every row: '64 16 45 135 Required', '48 12 45 135 Required', '32 16 90 270 Required' and '8 45 135 Required', '24 12 90 270 Required' and '6 45 135 Required', '16 8 90 270 Required', '12 6 90 270 Required', '8 4 90 270 Optional', '4 2 90 270 Optional'; and 'Quarter rate and free running clock only for 48 and 64 GT/s'. An earlier version of this row left out the 32 and 24 GT/s quarter-rate rows and wrongly said half rate below 48 GT/s.
claims.source_title: UCIe Consortium — overview deck, 2025, with the key metrics for UCIe 3.0

claims.statement: At 48 and 64 GT/s the transmitter offers six FFE presets, P0 to P5, with taps C(-1), C(0), C(+1) of (0, 1, 0), (-0.05, 0.95, 0), (0, 0.9, -0.1), (-0.05, 0.85, -0.1), (0, 0.8, -0.2) and (-0.05, 0.75, -0.2), each to within 0.025; training picks the preset with the best receive eye margin.
claims.source: UCIe Consortium overview deck (2025)
claims.conditions: 48 and 64 GT/s
claims.note: Deck, 'Training and Equalization at 48/64 GT/s': 'TX Preset selection (of 6) is accomplished in RXDESKEW phase', 'Pick best Preset based on RX Eye Margin', and the preset table with accuracy +/- 0.025.
claims.source_title: UCIe Consortium — overview deck, 2025, with the key metrics for UCIe 3.0

claims.statement: At 48 and 64 GT/s the power target is 0.5 to 0.75 pJ/b, broken down as about 40% transmitter, 40% receiver and 20% common circuits.
claims.source: UCIe Consortium overview deck (2025)
claims.conditions: Targets, not measurements
claims.note: Deck: 'Power Target: 0.5 - 0.75pJ/b Break down: ~ 40% TX, 40% RX, 20% common circuits'.
claims.source_title: UCIe Consortium — overview deck, 2025, with the key metrics for UCIe 3.0

claims.statement: UCIe 3.0 lets the transmitter, as well as the receiver, adjust clock-to-data skew during runtime recalibration, reusing the wider range it has from link initialization, to save power.
claims.source: UCIe Consortium overview deck (2025)
claims.conditions: UCIe 3.0

Replaces an unsourced CEM split (3.5 / 17.0 / 1.5 / 9.5 / 3.5 / 1.0 dB) and OCP/EDSFF figures the page carried until 15 Oct 2026.
